description: The registered process returns an accepted job receipt in data.job_id and data.status=queued. Retain that exact canonical id and read service_interface::job_service::get_job until terminal. The stored job.result is the original operation envelope, including data and structured error; job.error is also retained on failure. A receipt does not establish a session, dispatch row, or successful first turn. launch_busy names the current operation/job and starts no work. Coordinator-side causal decision surface. Actor identity is not a parameter: the server derives the registered instance/session from authenticated call context and verifies its exact current session/instance binding as the session holder of spawned_by_role. For an existing assigned dispatch, a verified successor in a different logical session may resolve it; the original spawned_by identity and assignment remain immutable provenance. Current authority is checked again on duplicate replay. Prospective creation still requires the original spawning instance. Supported actions are request_retry, resolve_blocker, accept_completion, reject_completion, cancel, cancel_legacy_expiry, and accept_verified_legacy_completion. request_retry is explicit and idempotent under the same dispatch_id from uptake_uncertain, failed_start, worker_lost, or expired; retry rearms only uptake/report/watchdog obligations and omits retired lifetime fields. resolve_blocker returns an authorized blocker to active after its ruling. reject_completion returns completion_reported to active for evidence repair. cancel records a normal terminal reason. cancel_legacy_expiry is restricted to legacy expired rows and requires durable no-live-attempt/work-preservation evidence with references. accept_verified_legacy_completion is restricted to legacy expired rows and binds the exact artifact hash, completion-contract digest, full worker evidence/verdict, independent acceptance evidence/verdict, and worker-evidence digest before reaching completed. Every action carries event_id, prior_version, and payload; duplicates are idempotent and stale or unauthorized decisions remain rejected audit events.
embedding_description: Submit a bounded session-launch job and retrieve its final result by exact job id. Make the coordinator decision for a durable worker lane: resolve a blocker, request one bounded replacement attempt, accept or reject exact completion evidence, or cancel within authority. The acceptance action is the only way a managed dispatch becomes completed.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Accepted submission only: data.job_id and data.status=queued. After terminal retrieval, job.result.data carries the original operation fields; job.result.error preserves its error. Continue dependent actions only after this retrieval.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report acceptance with job_id. Retrieve the terminal job before reporting an instance, dispatch state, first-turn outcome, or qualification verdict. Keep uptake_pending and uptake_uncertain distinct from worker ACK.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Checks event idempotency and causal version, validates that the requested action is legal from the current dispatch state, applies one CAS transition, and appends the coordinator decision. Completion acceptance performs a fresh filesystem read and hash before the state update.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: coordinator_authority_denied means the authenticated caller does not exactly match the current session holder of the dispatch coordinator role, or a prospective creation did not come from the original spawning instance. Historical original-session data is not required for assigned-dispatch resolution. *_not_allowed means the current state cannot take that action. stale_dispatch_version means another event won the race and this rejected decision remains auditable. legacy expiry evidence failures mean the restricted correction did not prove its disposition. completion artifact/hash/contract/evidence/verdict/worker-evidence errors mean independent acceptance failed and the dispatch did not complete. A replacement host error leaves the same dispatch_id in supervised failed_start.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Read managed_dispatch_status and decide from the fresh version. Reject or repair completion evidence rather than overriding validation. Route operator-only authority gaps to the operator; this verb does not grant capabilities or authorize Git/live-state mutation.
